The built environment industry is facing a major challenge in the next 20 years in adapting to a carbon-constrained city, where the built environment is expected to be more efficient in terms of resource use, carbon emission, and waste generation, and to provide a more sustainable living environment.

the built environment industry will need to adapt to meet new sustainability challenges and that the drivers of change facing it are: the increasing cost and scarcity of resources, the increasing costs of energy and water, the need to reduce carbon emissions and the need to improve the energy efficiency of buildings and the built environment.

the industry needs to change its business models, working practices, skills and knowledge base, design and construction processes, procurement and contractual arrangements, and the institutional structures in which it operates.

the built environment industry is facing a major challenge in adapting to the drivers of change that will be required to meet the sustainability goals for the next twenty years.

the industry needs to change the way it does business, the way it is organised, the skills it has available, the way it designs and constructs, the way it manages and maintains and the way it is regulated.

there is a clear need for a more holistic and integrated approach to the built environment, with a greater emphasis on whole-life performance and the development of more integrated design and construction processes.

the industry will need to undergo substantial change in its organisation and practices, and that this change will be driven not only by changes in technology but also in the institutional structures within which the industry operates.
